subject: Request: Activate rollback gate for model-9x after p95 spike (BrightPay)
messages:
From: Michael Hobbs <michael.hobbs@brightpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: spike in p95 for model-9x impacting live payroll runs

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a sudden spike in p95 response times from model-9x starting around 08:45 PST that correlates with our bulk payroll batch runs. Median latencies look okay but p95 jumped from ~220ms to 1.8s and some requests are timing out at 5s. This is causing queued jobs in our pipeline to slip and some customers reported timeouts.

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side regression? We need an ETA for mitigation — we've paused a few large customer runs but the backlog is growing.

I've attached a quick trace and a CSV of sample request IDs.

Thanks,
Michael Hobbs
Platform Ops | BrightPay

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:49:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: spike in p95 for model-9x impacting live payroll runs

Folks — forwarding BrightPay's alert. TL;DR: p95 for model-9x jumped to ~1.8s during their bulk runs; some timeouts at 5s. BrightPay is on a tight payroll schedule (deal DP-2034). They asked whether this is a regression on our side and for mitigation ETA.

Initial check of metrics shows a notable increase in KV cache misses concurrent with a small uptick in tail sequence length for this workspace. We rolled a kernel tweak to the canary pool earlier today (model-9x kernel v2 -> v3) which might have changed scheduling priorities under burst.

Proposal: request authorization to activate the rollback gate to model-9x:v2 on BrightPay's traffic slice and enable an immediate traffic pin for their API key. Rollback would take ~8 minutes to cutover with a short routing flap; expected p95 restoration to ~230-260ms based on previous metrics.

Attachments: runbook-revert-model-9x-v1.pdf (internal revert runbook), p95_spike_20251130.png (from BrightPay)

Requesting quick approval from Marcus / Grace — this is a revenue-impacting customer and we should avoid escalating to execs if we can remediate quickly. If you approve, I'll notify BrightPay and schedule the revert window immediately.

Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Approved to activate rollback gate on BrightPay's slice. Conditions:
- Perform rollback to model-9x:v2 with traffic pin as Naomi described.
- Execute during next 15-minute maintenance window (start no later than 10:30 PST).
- Run the quick verification checklist from the revert runbook and watch for CPU/GPU saturations and queue depth.
- If p95 doesn't drop below 400ms within 20 minutes, escalate to on-call runtime lead and prepare to open an incident bridge.

Ben, please stand by to help coordinate the routing change. Naomi, proceed to notify BrightPay and schedule the short cutover. Keep logs and attach the verification screenshot to this thread.

Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: spike in p95 for model-9x impacting live payroll runs

Michael — thanks for the alert and the trace. We have authorization to activate a rollback gate for your traffic slice to model-9x:v2 and to pin your API key to that variant.

Planned immediate steps (start 10:20 PST):
- 10:20: enable rollback gate and start routing 100% of BrightPay traffic to model-9x:v2 (expected cutover 8 ± 2 minutes).
- 10:30: run verification checklist (p95, error-rate, CPU/GPU, queue depth).
- 10:40: follow-up with initial verification screenshot.

Attachments included: runbook-revert-model-9x-v1.pdf (internal), post-cutover checklist snippet.

If anything changes from your side (additional bulk runs), flag immediately in this thread and we'll pause the cutover. Otherwise, we expect p95 to return to the 220–300ms band and will update when complete.

—
